genesis_challenges.name: Devnet Pilot — Fibonacci Discovery
genesis_challenges.verification_criteria: Compute Fibonacci(n) for n derived from challenge_id seed (range 100-200). Submit SHA256 of decimal string representation as output_hash. Verifiers reproduce n = 100 + (SHA256(challenge_id+'fib')[0:16] as uint64) % 101, then check SHA256(str(fib(n)).encode()).

genesis_challenges.name: Devnet Crypto — Hash Pre-image Search
genesis_challenges.verification_criteria: Find an input x = 'qcb-preimage-{N}' such that SHA256(x) starts with nibble 0 (4 leading zero bits). Submit SHA256(x) as output_hash. Starting nonce N = SHA256(challenge_id+'preimage')[0:16] as uint64 & 0xFFFFFFFF. Verifiers check output_hash starts with '0'.

genesis_challenges.name: Devnet Perf — Matrix Multiply Benchmark
genesis_challenges.verification_criteria: Run 16×16 integer matrix multiply (seeded from challenge_id). Seed = SHA256(challenge_id+'matmul')[0:16] as uint64 & 0xFFFF. Entries mod 997; compute diagonal sum of C=A×B mod 2^31. Submit SHA256('matmul-16x16-seed{S}-diag{D}') as output_hash.

genesis_challenges.name: Devnet Lattice — Shortest Vector Problem (4-dim)
genesis_challenges.verification_criteria: Find shortest non-zero vector in the 4-dimensional integer lattice with basis B derived from challenge_id seed. Seed = SHA256(challenge_id+'lattice')[0:16] as uint64. Build 4×4 basis using LCG (mult=6364136223846793005, add=1442695040888963407, entries = (state>>32)%31 - 15). Exhaustively search coefficient vectors in [-6,6]^4; find minimum non-zero ||Bv||^2. Submit SHA256('svp-dim4-seed{S}-vec{V}-norm{N}') as output_hash. Any verifier can reproduce B and check the submitted vector is genuinely shortest.

genesis_challenges.name: Devnet Primes — Prime Counting Function π(n)
genesis_challenges.verification_criteria: Compute π(n) — number of primes ≤ n — for challenge-seeded n. n = 10000 + (SHA256(challenge_id+'primes')[0:16] as uint64) % 40001, so 10000 ≤ n ≤ 50000. Submit SHA256('pi(n)={count}') as output_hash. Verifiers run a sieve and check pi_n independently.
